decision: Kept Diego node set: 103 named physical components plus BUS-SY230, BUS-AUX13A, BUS-AUX13B, BUS-NON1, BUS-416A, BUS-416B, BUS-416C, BUS-416D, and GND-GRID for 112 total nodes.

decision: Excluded train boundary labels, RAT-A/B, SAF A-D, ATS-A/B NORM/ALT, ESF-K labels, cable/drawing notes, and anonymous WN-* wire nodes from matrix nodes.
evidence: These are route or enclosure annotations in the raw visual; they do not appear as boxed physical components or named conductor endpoint rails.

decision: Retained direct named-endpoint adjacency for offsite/grid/generator sources, BUS-SY230, auxiliary bus tie, four 4.16 kV safety buses/ties, 480 V transformers/load centers/MCCs, ATS sources, and DC/UPS/48 V chains.
evidence: Solid feeders with filled terminal dots connect the named components/rails; crossings without filled dots were not converted to adjacency.

decision: Kept BUS-NON1 as a true named logical bus and retained BUS-AUX13A--BUS-NON1 and BUS-NON1--TR-SAF-C at medium confidence.
evidence: Raw crop shows BUS-NON1 as a thick labeled non-safety 13.8 kV service bus. Its left end ties by vertical drop to the BUS-AUX13A segment, and its right end lands at a filled TR-SAF-C terminal; geometry near CB-TIE13/TR-SAF-C keeps both uncertain.

decision: Removed Diego JB-RLY-A/B to relay fan-out edges; retained only visible CP/relay/instrument/control paths that terminate on named components, with ambiguous long-trunk cases marked uncertain.
evidence: The control bay has terminal dots on CP-ESFAS panels, K/UV/LOOP relays, and instrument racks. JB-RLY to relay fan-outs rely on broad relay-power trunk membership and do not show clean direct endpoint-to-endpoint terminations.

decision: Kept GND-GRID in the matrix but only as low-confidence grounding-reference connectivity; did not allow it to imply power/control adjacency among grounded devices.
evidence: Legend defines dotted grounding conductor and raw labels a bottom station ground grid with dotted drops. These are protective/reference connections, not feeder or control paths.

decision: Retained MCC-1C2--FAN-CRHV-A and MCC-1D2--FAN-CRHV-B at medium confidence, not high.
evidence: The fan feeders are visually near the ATS-B NORM/ALT vertical routes. There is plausible solid load wiring from the MCC areas, but route overlap prevents a high-confidence call.

decision: Removed 8 Diego edges: JB-RLY-A--RELAY-K1A, JB-RLY-A--RELAY-K2A, JB-RLY-A--RELAY-UV-A, JB-RLY-A--RELAY-LOOP-C, JB-RLY-B--RELAY-K1B, JB-RLY-B--RELAY-K2B, JB-RLY-B--RELAY-UV-B, JB-RLY-B--RELAY-LOOP-D. Added no new edges.
evidence: All eight were low-confidence inferred dashed relay-power fan-outs without visually isolated endpoint-to-endpoint terminations.

decision: Remaining uncertain retained cases are BUS-NON1 tie/termination, fan feeders near ATS-B routes, long PNL-DC to CP-ESFAS control-power trunks, CP-to-UV/LOOP relay paths, and low-confidence grounding-reference edges.
evidence: Each is visibly plausible on the raw schematic but involves trunked, dotted, dashed, or nearby crossing geometry that should not be upgraded without stronger endpoint evidence.
